target_customer: Young urban Indians renting cars and bikes by the hour or day, and vehicle owners or fleet partners listing vehicles
problem: Owning a car or two wheeler in Indian cities was costly and rentals were hard to book. JustRide, later Drivezy, offered on demand vehicle rental and sharing from an app.
business_model: Marketplace and own fleet rental revenue per trip, later franchise operated locations
product_category: Car and bike sharing and rental marketplace

founders.name: Abhishek Mahajan
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; PwC India from an Inc42 profile snippet.

founders.name: Ashwarya Pratap Singh
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and Inc42.

founders.name: Vasant Verma
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and Inc42.

founders.name: Amit Sahu
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Inc42 (2020-03); not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Zoomcar
competitors.what: Self drive car rental in Indian cities
competitors.traction_then: 250 pickup spots across six cities in July 2015
competitors.funding_then: $11 million round in July 2015 after $8 million in October 2014, Sequoia led

technical_complexity.rationale: A rental marketplace with bookings, vehicle availability and later IoT or key handoff was standard engineering with operational complexity in fleet and utilisation.

defensibility.rationale: Supply was rented or partner owned and customers multi-homed across Zoomcar, Ola and local rentals, so switching costs were low.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zoomcar was already funded by Sequoia and Ford; Inc42 (2020-03) says Bounce and Zoomcar approached Drivezy about M&A after the failed 2019 round, which Drivezy did not pursue.

market_need_then: Inc42 (2020-03) says the founders saw in 2014 that young Indians preferred on demand rentals to ownership; competitor funding in 2014 and 2015 shows investors saw demand.

identity.logo: A new logo was unveiled at the 2017 rebrand; Punekar News says it symbolizes continuous evolution as a service company, no visual detail given

rebrands.why: Inc42 says the name change came as the company moved from aggregator to marketplace and two wheelers were added; waiting a year was chosen because it was too early for people to associate JustRide with a new brand

brand_strength.rationale: Regional brand known in Indian rental coverage; no sources on merch, community or virality. The rebrand was an effort to match the new marketplace model rather than a growth driver.

pivots.why: Inc42 notes leasing around 250 cars proved expensive

pivots.to: Cars and two wheelers under the Drivezy name

pivots.why: Cost cutting after the failed Series C

outcome_analysis: Drivezy raised seed money in 2015 and 2016, joined YC in 2016 and raised a $20 million Series B plus $100 million asset financing in 2018, but the asset heavy rental model strained cash and founders went without salaries from 2018 to 2019. A reported $100 million Series C with SoftBank and Amazon did not close in 2019, the company pivoted to franchising and a secondary blog says the missed round plus COVID ended it; no primary source confirms a shutdown date.
notes: Drivezy website did not resolve during fetch (DNS failure), treated as dead or unreachable. The Series A rests on a single database (Seedtable, October 2017, $10M); CB Insights shows a Series A in October 2017 with no amount. YourStory states total equity of $31 million by 2018-11, which exceeds the rounds recorded (about $22.4M), so roughly $8.6M of equity is unaccounted for. The $100M asset financing is debt, not equity. The Series B and total came from YourStory search snippets; the full article was blocked. The shutdown claim rests on a secondary blog, startupfeed.in, and exit type stays unknown. Inc42 also reports talks for $30M from a Middle East fund and Shell, outcome unknown. Zoomcar is the only competitor with a source dated before the batch.
